newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans lower on USDA but weather supportive.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans lower on USDA but weather supportive.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures opened lower on Monday, hit by news USDA left unchanged at 125 million bushels its 1996-97 ending stocks projection, but forecasts for cool weather boosted November, traders said.

Dealers said news USDA had raised its projection for soybean imports in 1996/97 to 10 million bushels from five million a month earlier would heighten concern about a possible pick-up in shipments from South America.
Many analysts had been looking for USDA to cut its soybean ending stocks figure by between five and ten million. USDA increased its soybean crush estimate to 1.425 billion.

USDA also pegged 1997 U.S. soybean production at a record 2.6 billion bushels which pushed new crop November down early. But Novemer traded on both sides amid forecasts for cool, wet weather in the U.S. Midwest which may delay plantings.

In opening trade, locals were aggressive sellers and LIT sold one million bushels July. ADM, Cargill Investor Services and Refco Inc each bought 0.5 million bushels July. ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp bought 0.4 million November.
At 0952 CDT, soybeans were down three to 1/2 cent per bushel with July off three at $8.86.
